compiler_spec.ingestion: Ghidra decodes through its production DocumentStorage/XML parser inside BfdArchitecture::init. Rugra's fixture parses the locked text into the structured Element DOM (fixture-local, same model as cspec_param_model_1204.rs) and drives the production TreeDecoder through the mapped decode functions; production cspec text ingestion remains CSPEC-TEXT-INGEST-0001's MISMATCH.

analysis_options.document_selection: The complete locked x86-64-gcc.cspec is ingested on the C++ side; observations select the <data_organization> subtree (real production bytes including skipped machine_alignment/default_alignment/default_pointer_alignment/short_size/long_long_size/float_size/double_size/long_double_size children) plus seven synthetic <data_organization> documents.
analysis_options.arch_inputs: C++ observes setupSizes' Architecture lookups live (default size 8, stack spacebase size 8 via RSP, default data space ram address size 8, no far-pointer segment op) and serializes them. Rust receives the same values as locked-spec constants in the fixture; live Architecture input derivation is not wired on the Rust side.
analysis_options.setup_model: The C++ 'production' group is the real chain (init -> parseCompilerConfig -> decodeDataOrganization -> setupSizes). The Rust 'production' group emulates it as decode_data_organization(production element) + setup_sizes(locked arch inputs); the byte diff pins both to the same factory state.
analysis_options.normalization: No ids, orders, values, or exception texts are normalized. The alignment map is observed through getAlignment probes (sizes 0..17 production/raw, per-case ranges) because alignMap is private; the empty-map LowlevelError text is compared verbatim.

cases.production: Full BfdArchitecture::init chain on the locked spec set and curl binary; the architecture factory's six sizes plus getAlignment probes 0..17 and getPrimitiveAlignSize probes 1..17 after parseCompilerConfig + setupSizes.
cases.raw_decode: Standalone TypeFactory decoding the production <data_organization> element pre-setupSizes: char stays 0 (no defaulting at decode), align[0] stays -1.
cases.c1_sparse_map: Synthetic map with entries at sizes 3 and 7 only: forward fill from nearest earlier explicit value, indices 0..2 keep -1/1/1.
cases.c2_empty_map: Empty <size_alignment_map>: oracle LowlevelError text from getAlignment, then setupSizes installs setDefaultAlignmentMap (align[0] == 0).
cases.c3_zero_entry: Explicit <entry size="0">: align[0] becomes observable (1) and getPrimitiveAlignSize(0) is a safe probe returning 0.
cases.c4_duplicate_zero_align: Out-of-order entries with a later duplicate size=8 winning and an explicit alignment=0 kept; no primitive probes (align 0 divides by zero in the oracle).
cases.c5_char_only_setup: Only <char_size value="3"> decoded; setupSizes derives int 4 (stack 8 clamped), long 8, wchar 2, pointer 8, default map.
cases.c6_unknown_children_setup: machine_alignment/default_alignment/short_size/float_size/double_size skipped around one consumed integer_size=2; int != 4 makes sizeOfLong copy 2 instead of 8.
cases.c7_negative_setup: integer_size=-2 survives decode as int4 and flows through sizeOfLong = (int==4) ? 8 : int.
cases.c8_sam_followed_by_child: Synthetic document with <size_alignment_map> followed by <char_size value="3">: children after the map are still consumed (oracle sam branch falls through to closeElement, type.cc:4604-4612); char reads 3 and align probes [-1,1] on both sides. Added in the review rework: a stray continue used to leave Rugra's TreeDecoder on the map element and silently drop the trailing child.

observation_schema.format: One compact UTF-8 JSON object with fixed key and array order plus final newline.
observation_schema.sizes: The six persisted size fields (int/long/char/wchar/pointer/alt_pointer) via the getSizeOf* getters.
observation_schema.align: getAlignment probes reconstructing the private alignMap slot by slot, including the >= size fallback to the last entry and the -1 sentinel at index 0.
observation_schema.primitive: getPrimitiveAlignSize probes (sizeof-style padding), including size 17 padding to 32 under a 16-byte alignment.
observation_schema.errors: Verbatim oracle LowlevelError text for the uninitialized alignment map.

coverage.production_cspec_data_organization_state: MATCH: six sizes plus 18 alignment and 17 primitive probes of the real init chain, byte-identical.
coverage.raw_decode_pre_setup_state: MATCH: decode stores parsed values only; absent char_size leaves char 0; align[0] is -1.
coverage.sparse_forward_fill_and_index0_minus1: MATCH: fill starts at index 1 with curAlign 1; index 0 keeps -1.
coverage.empty_map_error_and_default_install: MATCH: verbatim 'TypeFactory alignment map not initialized', empty map stays empty through decode, setupSizes installs [0,1,2,2,4,4,4,4,8].
coverage.explicit_zero_entry_and_primitive_zero: MATCH: explicit size-0 entry sets align[0]=1; getPrimitiveAlignSize(0) returns 0.
coverage.duplicate_entry_and_zero_alignment: MATCH: later duplicate size entry wins; explicit alignment=0 preserved by the fill pass.
coverage.unknown_children_skip: MATCH: machine_alignment/default_alignment/short_size/float_size/double_size children consumed-and-skipped without touching state.
coverage.post_sam_child_consumption: MATCH: children following <size_alignment_map> are consumed after the unified close (c8: char_size after sam reads 3; align [-1,1]). Fixed in review rework — the sam branch previously skipped close_element, leaving the decoder stack on the map and dropping trailing children (Ghidra reads 3, old Rugra read 0).
coverage.setup_sizes_derivation: MATCH: int from stack spacebase clamped to 4, long via the (int==4)?8:int branch, char 1, wchar 2, pointer from default data space address size, default map install.
coverage.negative_signed_sizes: MATCH: readSignedInteger values survive as int4 (-2) through decode and setup.
coverage.primitive_align_size_padding: MATCH: unsigned 32-bit modulo semantics of size % align reproduced (17 pads to 32).
coverage.enum_config_state: UNTESTED: enumsize/enumtype are private with no oracle getters; parseEnumConfig state exists on both sides but is not serializable from the locked C++ class.
coverage.architecture_input_derivation: UNTESTED: Rust setup_sizes receives locked-spec constants; the live glb->getStackSpace/getDefaultDataSpace/getSegmentOp lookups have no Rugra Architecture wiring yet.
coverage.illformed_non_entry_child_in_map: MISMATCH (conservative): on a non-<entry> child Ghidra breaks leaving the element open; only debug-assert builds (CPUI_DEBUG) diagnose the mis-nested parent close, and release-build stream positions are not proven divergent from Rugra's close-and-skip. No equivalence proof exists for either build mode, the path is unreachable via well-formed compiler specs, and it is not exercised by this fixture.
coverage.get_primitive_align_size_zero_alignment: UNTESTED: alignment 0 is a division by zero (SIGFPE in the oracle, panic in Rust); abnormal termination on both sides, not serializable.
coverage.production_rugra_cspec_text_ingestion: MISMATCH: the Rust fixture builds the Element DOM locally; production XML text ingest into parse_compiler_config is CSPEC-TEXT-INGEST-0001's residual.

overall_status: MISMATCH: every declared observation (production state, raw decode state, all seven synthetic cases, error text, and all probe arrays) is byte-identical to locked Ghidra 12.0.4 output. Residuals: enum state unobservable in the oracle, live architecture-input derivation unwired on Rust, ill-formed non-entry map children diverge (unreachable via well-formed specs), zero-alignment primitive queries abort on both sides, and production text ingestion remains the text-ingest domain's mismatch.
